how: Members recruit fellow dwarves and request help with particular additions to the shared display.
Willing novices ask how to draw and contribute, and others explain choosing a color and placing it.
A notice explains the changed five-minute interval without establishing its effect on participation.
A request for help on the dead goblin receives a brief acceptance framed as a reassigned task.
Members judge available space, coordination, and defensible scale insufficient for some proposed extensions.
A sharp coordination order receives an inclusion request, but neither personal withdrawal from pixel work nor completed quarrel repair is established.
Members initiate work by setting an anchor, carving out a corner, and proposing profession-colored figures.
Contributors revise figures, assign professions, change priorities, and drop a proposal in favor of work already underway.
Members choose between a short redirect name and the full subreddit name for identifying the work.
Members report completed parts and individual progress, including a mug, one lettering pixel, and an unfinished sign.
Anchor coordinates, a proposed grid, and visible goal images make contributions locatable and comparable.
Changed targets must reach relevant placers through accessible public images when the planning chat is unavailable.
Planning moves into chat and returns through reported decisions, expansion limits, diplomatic invitations, and ally-colored targets.
A member also asks the public thread to carry a relocation proposal into chat, making the relay bidirectional.
Chat coordination reaches willing contributors only when its goals also become accessible to people unable to use the chat.
Repairers need a visible revised goal to distinguish intended changes from an invasion they would otherwise repair away.
Members recruit script users, propose defensive adjustments, and debate automation's fun and usefulness during sleep.
Sleep is invoked to justify automated upkeep, while another contributor reports being pulled away after placing a few pixels.
Members report a site-imposed wait and its later five-minute interval without demonstrating malfunction or extra-pixel exploitation.
Deliberate coordination can consist of reported decisions about repair and expansion without documented formal offices or elections.
Reported decisions in one room cannot test the stated cross-room prevalence of decided order.
Using a planning chat does not by itself establish secret plans, infiltration, or spying on rivals.
Members clean, repair, and defend figures against changed colors, encroachment, and the Void.
The revised known-form mechanism fits a repairer undoing an intended edit after mistaking it for invasion.
Apply demonstrated mistaken restoration without inferring eventual loss or abandonment when unreached keepers' outcomes remain unobserved.
Independent visual maintenance can continue without participation in any coordination channel.
Participants identify friendly fire and mistakes when apparently hostile pixels belong to an intended design.
Neighbors negotiate reciprocal noninterference, conditional borders, truces, and proposed relocation or rebuilding.
Members welcome neighbors, remind placers to respect agreements, urge returning disputed art, and stop repairing an intended recoloring.
Neighbors offer joint defense, barter construction help for preserved pixels, and ask for help for nearby allies.
An alliance inquiry, reported collaboration, and an ally-colored plan show cooperation through named partners and shared designs.
A member reports carrying a conditional border agreement back from another group's thread.
Territorial requests and reciprocal boundaries do not establish continuing host authority over a guest work.
Members locate initial work, try coordinates, propose shifting a row, and seek uses for small remaining spaces without establishing prior destruction.
Movement and rebuilding proposals do not establish both triggering erasure and a completed collective relocation.
A member justifies sparing other structures through a creators-rather-than-destroyers norm without establishing consensus.
Choosing another project while wishing these builders well does not establish explicitly divided membership in a contest.
Agreement reports and access objections show no explicit disclaimer of standing, refusal to be bound, or request for an authorized representative.
Game language supplies forms for recruitment, arrival, task acceptance, restraint, and calls to defend the work.
An admitted joke alteration is bargained over, while a canvas collision becomes a game-style engraving.
Applying inherited lore to a canvas opponent does not establish a pre-canvas relationship that selected that opponent.
Territorial conflict and fandom insults do not establish an earlier quarrel with the same neighbors.
Creating a short redirect for an existing community does not establish a new collective formed around a mark.
A hostile term's presence does not establish an objection to that term or collective policing of offensive language.
Temporary permission, megathread proposals, spam complaints, defenses of relevance, and unsubscribing contest the host's boundary around canvas talk.
One participant explicitly attributes claimed destructive assistance to irritation with canvas posting in the host sub.
The evidence establishes a participant's stated motive and claimed assistance, without independent pixel measurement or evidence of collective host opposition.
Host posting irritation is explicitly offered as a reason for helping destructive canvas action.
A canvas joke and a temporary posting rule do not establish deceptive host-wide April Fools framing.
Participants announce completion, thank contributors, and name the finished work.
Participants share a timelapse and recount conflicts, treaties, concessions, and the finished display.
A post-close report of contributed pixels records earlier assistance rather than demonstrating new placement after the stop.
Reported arrivals for the event channel are welcomed into the broader organizing chat.
A short redirect is created to make the game findable, while actual discovery through that route remains unmeasured.
Distinguish reported event-channel arrivals from artwork-driven subreddit discovery and lasting membership conversion.
A pre-close welcome does not establish a later decision or durable outcome about retaining the temporary effort.
Final naming, war recollections, and a concession report do not establish contested cleanup or correction of the room's public history.
Finishing a figure for a game's deity does not demonstrate seeking acknowledgment from creators, teams, streamers, or press.
Members call a joint strike against a neighboring flag, while a separate participant admits a joke alteration.
Insults, marching imagery, and a claimed memorial to an opponent's defeat carry conflict into talk.
A lettering request receives a direct report of a pixel contributed to that lettering.
Starting and calling can coincide in one opening rather than requiring distinct sequential turns.
An invitation to build and maintain a figure is followed by a stated need to concentrate on cleaning it.
Keeping existing pixels can overlap initial construction rather than wait for the entire display to be completed.
A perceived neighboring threat receives an accommodation and joint-defense offer directly.
A reported agreement receives a direct welcome and later reminders to leave the neighboring logo alone.
Overnight coverage is an explicit automation rationale, while the proposed manual-capacity threshold remains unmeasured.
An ally-pattern plan receives a repairer's assent and a completion announcement within the same thread.
Recording can accompany construction when a timelapse is shared before later pieces are completed.
Recording and completion accounts do not establish celebration as the cause of recording.
The pre-close welcome is not linked to the timelapse or final accounts as the cause of a later retention decision.
Capacity objections and relocation proposals do not establish that insufficient hands caused a completed collective move.
Design proposals, an anchor, and a grid proposal do not establish a template settling a preceding design dispute.
The dead-goblin help request receives a brief acceptance that asks for nothing back.
The observed assent supports a written response without testing normative obligation, refusal preferences, or silent placement answers.
Joint-defense offers and requests for neighbor help do not establish shortage of hands as their cause.
Accommodation and offered help can occur in the same turn rather than as separately observed stages.
Earlier recruitment and later strike calls do not identify recruits becoming attackers because of the first call.
Restraint proposals and retrospective rebuilding do not establish the proposed reasoned-refusal mechanism as a direct answer to an attack call.
Bargaining during conflict is visible, while separate attack posts cannot be assigned as the cause of those negotiations.
Attack calls and rival-directed talk coexist without establishing that a particular call caused a subsequent taunt.
Joint defense is explicitly offered against shared threats, but the coalition's internal formation remains unseen.
Host complaints concern event content broadly and do not isolate recruitment calls as the sole cause of the flood.
The revised timing boundary cannot be tested because the coded passages show neither authority disclaimers during terms nor later refusals to be bound.
